head: 151f2866a
notes: Phase 3b: the app passes on missing history on a join and on reading, and every group decrypt retries when keys arrive. Adds C10.

instruments.evidence: e619a6d8c..151f2866a: 3b16b581e (the joiner also gets group_keys_shared), 6f2f4301d (the app passes on missing versions on a join and on every read of a group; the key cache keeps a generation that rises on every forget; text, media and pinned decrypts re-run on it; the socket context handles group_member_joined and group_keys_shared), 151f2866a (review: media and pinned retry tests). Boundaries: the two socket events, the history share request, the decrypt effects, the member list query.

Read b3df29afc (3a: the events and who receives them; it said 3b must drop the joiner's missing record), 7cf2b679d (C9, sender names), da9ed20de (the cache's forget rule: whoever grants a version must forget, or readers keep it missing -- the generation now makes the forget visible to the bubbles).

The history share request body, built with real RSA keys: {1: {99: copy}} when the newcomer lacks version 1 and this member holds it; nothing sent when missing_history is empty (groupKeyShareOnJoin.test, two inputs). The copy opens a message sealed before the join with the newcomer's private key.

Rendered in the pane as DERRF after the restart: 'Test' opens with every message and name, one GET /groups/47/keys and no history POST, since nobody lacks a version now. The retry is asserted on the rendered bubble text, the media hook's blob, and the pinned bar's text.
Socket frames read in the Go tests: group_member_joined to members and group_keys_shared to the joiner, for a direct add and an accepted invite.
Event names match: the Go handlers send group_member_joined and group_keys_shared; WebSocketContext switches on the same strings; payload key conversation_id on both.
The client reads payload.conversation_id, the field both events carry.

instruments.why: One share routine (shareMissingHistory) behind all three callers: the send path, the read path and the join event.
No untyped accessor beyond the payload cast, which the socket tests exercise.

instruments.evidence: The socket test sends the frames the Go tests read from the real hub: {type, payload: {conversation_id, user_id}}.
Siblings of the join share: groupKeyForSending already shared missing history on send; the read path and the join event now call the same routine.
The group branches of the three decrypt sites and both socket cases are each reached by a test.

A refused or failed share is logged and does not throw (shareMissingHistory catches); a second member sharing the same versions a moment later is refused by the server, which is logged noise, not a failure. The invite path remains the main one.
The retry dependency is one hook, useGroupKeysGeneration, used by all three sites.

Other one-shot group decrypts: the page's search map (decrypts only while a message search runs, and again when it changes), SearchResultsPage, the feed cards and mod mail. None holds a bubble a newcomer is looking at while keys arrive; they decrypt again on their next load.

instruments.why: No shared memory; the counter is single-threaded JS.

instruments.evidence: p3b-r1-media-and-pinned-retry-untested: with the media hook and pinned bar at their pre-3b state (a full revert, so tsc -b stays clean), both new tests fail waiting for the key-arrived result.
tsc -b and eslint clean on every changed file; go build, go vet (handlers, integration) and gofmt clean.
Finding 1's technique was not a row: remove each added line and require a test to notice. Added as C10.

instruments.why: The full flow needs two signed-in accounts, which I cannot sign into; the user tests invite, accept and reading. Unverified in a real browser until then, said to the user.

instruments.evidence: The read path starts the share while it opens this device's copies; the share decides by itself whether anything is missing and returns without a request when nothing is.
The generation is module state; only forgetGroupKeys changes it, and every change notifies the listeners.
Go runs with -v and TEST_DATABASE_URL: join, keys-shared and invite socket tests and 33 handler group tests PASS, 0 SKIP.

3b's promises: online members pass on missing versions on a join (yes); members who open the group later do it then (yes, read path); the newcomer's app drops its missing record and the old messages open without a reload (yes, via group_keys_shared to the joiner and the generation).

Three entry points can run the share: the send path, the read path, the join event. Two can overlap in one app (a join while the group is being read); the server serializes on the conversation row and refuses the second as already given, so no copy is written twice.

Ran every test that imports or mocks groupKeyCache, useDecryptedContent, useDecryptedMedia, PinnedMessagesBar or WebSocketContext: 16 files, 174 passed, 1 old skip. Two mocks of groupKeyCache became partial mocks for the new exports.

Earlier controls target message.go, MessagesPage.tsx, groups.go (the accept announcement line, unchanged here) and the blocking test; re-ran p3-r1-accept-join-untested's test after 3b16b581e: it still fails with the patch, since the invited case now also waits for the joiner's event.

instruments.why: No resource after an await; the listener set is cleared by unsubscribe.
Frontend tests; the socket side is tested on the real hub.

instruments.evidence: Shuffled the four changed test files (seed 23): 58 passed.
Producers of group_keys_shared: rotation with history, ShareHistory, and a join (to the joiner). Producers of group_member_joined: add and accept. The client consumes both.
Found finding 1: removed each added line in turn. The share on read, the generation rise, the text retry, and the three socket-handler lines each failed a test; the media and pinned retries did not.

findings.summary: The key-generation retry was added to three decrypt sites and tested on one; removing it from the media hook or the pinned bar left every test green.
